hunks.baseline: I had already checked the Quest window countless times.
hunks.sol: I’d checked the Quest window several times already.

hunks.baseline: I stared at the translucent holographic window as if I could bore a hole through it, but no miracle occurred that changed the words written on the final line.
hunks.sol: I glared at the translucent hologram, but the words on the last line refused to change.

hunks.baseline: This was not the first time.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t the first time.

hunks.baseline: From the moment I first set foot in the Murim until now, I had received this kind of goddamn Quest several times. Of course, in the beginning, I had been utterly dumbfounded.
hunks.sol: Since setting foot in Murim, I’d been given more than a few goddamn Quests like this. The first time, of course, I’d been stunned.

hunks.baseline: I had fought countless battles while working as a Hunter, but death had always frightened me.
hunks.sol: I’d fought countless battles as a Hunter, but death had always frightened me. Or rather, what frightened me was everything I’d have to leave behind.

hunks.baseline: More precisely, it would be more accurate to say that I was afraid of everything I would have to leave behind, rather than death itself.
At least if I died in a Gate, my family would receive some kind of death benefit. If I died in the Murim, there would be nothing.
hunks.sol: At least if I died in a Gate, my family would get a death benefit. If I died in Murim, they’d get nothing.

hunks.baseline: Of course, there was an unbridgeable gap between the me of those days and the me I was now.
With every crisis, my guts were forcibly injected with Botox and grew bigger by the day, while my body and mind toughened in proportion.
hunks.sol: Still, there was no comparing who I’d been then to who I was now. Every crisis had given my guts a forced Botox injection. They’d grown bigger by the day, and my body and mind had toughened along with them.

hunks.baseline: *I’ve never been in a situation like this before.*
hunks.sol: *I’ve never been in a situation like this.*

hunks.baseline: The reason I had managed to survive every time I stood at the crossroads between life and death was simple.
There had always been someone beside me who would fight alongside me, and whenever I had to face something alone, I had been ready to fight with my life on the line.
hunks.sol: There was a simple reason I’d survived every brush with death. I’d either had someone beside me to fight with, or, when I had to face an enemy alone, I’d been ready to put my life on the line.

hunks.baseline: And after struggling and thrashing until the very end, I had survived.
hunks.sol: I’d fought and struggled to the bitter end. And I’d survived.

hunks.baseline: At the very least, I had never been in a situation where I had enormous iron balls hanging all over my body while my internal energy was sealed.
hunks.sol: But never with enormous iron balls hanging all over my body and my internal energy sealed.

hunks.baseline: “……Damn it.”
hunks.sol: “…Damn it.”

hunks.baseline: I muttered under my breath and closed my eyes. The text written in the Quest description seemed to rise clearly in the darkness.
hunks.sol: I muttered under my breath and closed my eyes. The words from the Quest description seemed to appear against the darkness.

hunks.baseline: > **As long as you possess a strong Will and even a single thread of goodwill, a path to life will open.**
hunks.sol: *With a strong Will and even a single thread of goodwill, a path to life will open.*

hunks.baseline: The System occasionally sent me messages that I could not tell were hints or complete nonsense.
hunks.sol: The System sometimes sent me messages I couldn’t tell apart from hints or complete nonsense. Was this just encouragement? Or was it the clue I needed to escape?

hunks.baseline: In that sense, was this merely a word of encouragement? Or was it a decisive clue telling me how to escape the underground prison?

hunks.sol: As I sat there thinking with my eyes closed, liquid fell from above, struck the floor, and splashed onto the back of my hand.

hunks.baseline: It was too sticky to be groundwater, and its temperature was warm enough to make me feel grimy.
hunks.sol: Too sticky to be groundwater. Warm enough to make my skin crawl.

hunks.baseline: I opened my eyes at once, but without even looking at the ceiling, I spoke.
hunks.sol: I opened my eyes but didn’t bother looking up.

hunks.baseline: “……You crazy bastard. I told you not to drool so much.”
hunks.sol: “…You crazy bastard. I told you to quit drooling.”

hunks.baseline: Along with the sound of someone swallowing saliva—*slurp*—Taishan’s voice rang out.
hunks.sol: I heard a slurp as Taishan swallowed.

hunks.baseline: “Sorry. Taishan did that because Taishan too hungry.”
hunks.sol: “Sorry. Taishan was too hungry.”

hunks.baseline: “Then why is someone who’s hungry pressing his mouth against a hole in the floor? Just sit there quietly.”
hunks.sol: “If you’re hungry, why are you putting your mouth against a hole in the floor? Just sit still.”

hunks.baseline: “But if Taishan keeps licking, it’s surprisingly salty.”
hunks.sol: “But if Taishan keeps licking, it’s kind of salty.”

hunks.baseline: “Licking? Licking what?”
hunks.sol: “Licking? What?”

hunks.baseline: “Rock. This place is a rock restaurant.”
hunks.sol: “Rock. This place has good rock.”

hunks.baseline: “Crying out loud? Is that some kind of seasoning?”
hunks.sol: “Crying out loud? Is that some kind of sauce?”

hunks.baseline: *This crazy bastard……*
hunks.sol: *This crazy bastard…*

hunks.baseline: I swallowed the curse that had risen to my throat. Getting angry at him now would only drain my energy. It would not change anything.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the curse rising in my throat. Getting angry at him would only waste what little energy I had. It wouldn’t change anything.

hunks.baseline: Besides, Taishan’s situation was not very good, either.

I had no idea what sort of creature he was made of—his vital points were so thick that the Pressure-Point Strike hadn’t worked—but his internal energy had been sealed, and his whole body was bound. Even Taishan’s natural strength couldn’t get him out of that.

hunks.baseline: As I listened to his quiet whining echo through the prison, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
A thought that could be called guilt.
hunks.sol: Listening to his quiet whining, I suddenly felt something that could only be called guilt.

hunks.baseline: *All of this is my fault.*
hunks.sol: *This is all my fault.*

hunks.baseline: “……Hey, Taishan.”
hunks.sol: “…Hey, Taishan.”

hunks.baseline: “Pavilion Master called Taishan?”
hunks.sol: “Pavilion Master. Why did you call Taishan?”

hunks.baseline: As I spoke, I looked up at the ceiling. Through a hole about the size of a child’s fist, I saw one large, clear eye like a calf’s.
hunks.sol: I looked up as I spoke. Through a hole the size of a child’s fist, I could see one enormous, clear eye, like a calf’s.

hunks.baseline: It held a look of complete bewilderment.
hunks.sol: He had no idea what I meant.

hunks.baseline: I had always thought this, but Taishan possessed a pure heart that did not match his age or size. Like a clean, blank sheet of paper.
hunks.sol: I’d always thought Taishan had a heart far more innocent than his age or size suggested. He was like a clean sheet of paper.

hunks.baseline: I opened my mouth with a sigh.
hunks.sol: I sighed.

hunks.baseline: “I should have made a better judgment. But I didn’t. It was my mistake.”
hunks.sol: “I should’ve made a better call. I didn’t. I made a mistake.”

hunks.baseline: It had been a painful miscalculation. In terms of baduk, it had been a terrible move.
hunks.sol: A painful misjudgment. In baduk terms, a terrible move.

hunks.baseline: I had locked myself inside the underground prison to clean up the consequences of that mistake, but… damn it. I still had doubts about whether it had really been the right choice.
hunks.sol: I’d let them lock me in this prison to deal with the consequences, but… damn it. I still wasn’t sure that had been the right choice, either.

hunks.baseline: “Taishan okay.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan is okay.”

hunks.baseline: “Mm-hmm. Taishan really okay.”
hunks.sol: “Mm-hmm. Taishan is really okay.”

hunks.baseline: I closed my mouth and lowered my head. Taishan probably did not even understand how the current situation was unfolding.

hunks.sol: I lowered my head. He probably didn’t even understand what was happening. Right now, the most important thing to him was that he was hungry. The second most important was that he had no way to do anything about it.

hunks.baseline: *Yeah. Maybe that’s better for him.*
hunks.sol: *Maybe that’s better for him.*

hunks.baseline: But the next moment, when I heard what he said afterward, I realized something.
Taishan was far cleverer than I had thought.

hunks.baseline: “Pavilion Master doesn’t need to be sorry to Taishan.”
hunks.sol: “Pavilion Master doesn’t need to feel sorry for Taishan.”

hunks.baseline: Startled, I raised my head and looked at the ceiling. Taishan met my gaze and continued in a clear voice.
hunks.sol: I looked up in surprise. Taishan met my eyes and spoke clearly.

hunks.baseline: “Since Taishan was very young, people teased Taishan and called him stupid. Whenever they were bored, they came and hit Taishan. If Taishan hadn’t met Lord…… Taishan might still be getting hit and crying every day. Taishan had a very hard time.”
hunks.sol: “Ever since Taishan was little, people called him stupid and made fun of him. They came and hit him whenever they were bored. If Taishan hadn’t met Lord… maybe someone would still hit Taishan every day, and Taishan would cry. It was hard.”

hunks.baseline: His mood and manner of speaking were completely different from usual. I widened my eyes at this unfamiliar side of Taishan as his voice continued to reach me, smooth as flowing water.
hunks.sol: This wasn’t the Taishan I was used to. His whole manner had changed, and his words flowed without a pause as I stared up at him.

hunks.sol: “But Lord was different. Even when Taishan said something wrong, Lord understood. When Taishan ate a lot, Lord patted him on the back and told him to eat slowly. So Taishan decided to give his life to Lord.”

hunks.baseline: “You……”

Looking back now, Lord was right. A few days ago, it was the Pavilion Master who saved Lord in stupid Taishan’s place.”

hunks.baseline: “Taishan likes the Fire Dragon Pavilion now. Taishan likes little and cute Namho, Hyuk Mujin, who sometimes bothers Taishan, fierce Song Ilseom, and Ju Hwaran, who is as pretty as a flower. And Taishan likes the Pavilion Master second-most after Lord.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan likes the Fire Dragon Pavilion now. Taishan likes little, cute Namho, and Hyuk Mujin, even if he’s annoying sometimes. Taishan likes fierce Song Ilseom and Ju Hwaran, who’s pretty as a flower. And after Lord, Taishan likes Pavilion Master best.”

hunks.baseline: The eyes looking at me from beyond the hole curved gently.
hunks.sol: I was speechless. Beyond the hole, his eye curved gently.

hunks.baseline: “Taishan trusts Lord, and Lord trusts the Pavilion Master. So Pavilion Master, trust yourself. The Pavilion Master will definitely find a way. Just like always.”
hunks.sol: “Taishan trusts Lord. Lord trusts Pavilion Master. So Pavilion Master should trust himself. Pavilion Master will find a way. Just like always.”

hunks.baseline: I only stared blankly for a while as Taishan finished speaking and giggled.

hunks.baseline: I would never die. I could never die here.
